issue.definition_bad_row: Province {id} in definition.csv does not have three numeric colours: “{row}”.
issue.definition_duplicate_id: Province {id} is repeated in definition.csv (it was already on line {first}).
issue.definition_duplicate_color: Colour {color} of province {id} is already used by another province in definition.csv (line {first}): the game could not tell them apart on the map.
issue.bmp_size_mismatch: {file} is {width}×{height} and the province map is {expected_width}×{expected_height}.
explain.title.bmp_size_mismatch: Why: {file} is not the same size as the province map
explain.outcome.bmp_size_mismatch: The game overlays the layers pixel by pixel: with different sizes, terrain or rivers land on other provinces or the map fails to load.
explain.title.definition_duplicate_color: Why: Two provinces in definition.csv use colour {color}
explain.outcome.definition_duplicate_col: The game gives the pixels of that colour to only one of them: the other ends up with no land on the map.
explain.title.definition_duplicate_id: Why: Province {id} appears twice in definition.csv
explain.outcome.definition_duplicate_id: Only one row counts: the colour of the other one belongs to no province.
explain.title.definition_bad_row: Why: The row of province {id} does not have three numeric colours
explain.outcome.definition_bad_row: The game cannot place province {id} on the map: it has no colour to find its pixels.
issue.definition_bad_number: Province {province} in definition.csv has the number “{text}”: the game reads {value}.
explain.title.definition_bad_number: Why: “{text}” is not a clean number in the row of province {province}
explain.outcome.definition_bad_number: The game reads {value} and carries on: nothing breaks, but other programs may read it differently.
issue.province_without_pixels: Province {province} has a row in definition.csv but its colour is not on the map.
explain.title.province_without_pixels: Why: The colour of province {province} is not on the province map
explain.outcome.province_without_pixels: Province {province} exists for the game but covers no pixels: nobody will see it or be able to enter it.
issue.province_fragmented: Province {province} is split into {parts} pieces on the map.
explain.outcome.province_fragmented: The game treats it as a single province; stray pieces are usually pixels lost while drawing.
issue.max_provinces_too_small: max_provinces is {max} and the highest province is {largest}.
explain.title.max_provinces_too_small: Why: max_provinces ({max}) is not greater than the highest id ({largest})
explain.outcome.max_provinces_too_small: The game ignores provinces whose id is equal to or above max_provinces, or fails to load the map.
issue.sea_start_unknown: sea_starts names province {province}, which has no row in definition.csv.
explain.title.sea_start_unknown: Why: sea_starts includes province {province}, which does not exist
explain.outcome.sea_start_unknown: That value marks no sea: it is either unnecessary or a typo for another province.
explain.title.sea_start_duplicate: Why: Province {province} is repeated in sea_starts
explain.outcome.sea_start_duplicate: Nothing changes in game (it is still sea), but one of the occurrences is unnecessary.
explain.outcome.region_empty: A state with no provinces does not show up in game; it can be deleted or filled.
issue.region_not_contiguous: The provinces of state {region} do not touch: {apart} are cut off.
explain.title.region_not_contiguous: Why: State {region} is split into several areas
explain.outcome.region_not_contiguous: The game allows it (there are islands and exclaves), but it is often a province put in the wrong state.
issue.climate_layout: Climate {climate} has {entries} entries and {lists} province lists; it should have two entries and one list.
explain.title.climate_layout: Why: Climate {climate} does not have its pair of entries
explain.outcome.climate_layout: climate.txt uses two entries with the same name (modifiers and list): if one is missing, provinces lose their climate or the climate loses its effects.
issue.positions_missing: Province {province} has no block in positions.txt.
explain.outcome.positions_missing: The game places its units, name and buildings wherever it can, often outside the province.
issue.missing_history: Land province {province} has no file in history/provinces.
explain.outcome.missing_history: It starts the game with no owner, no RGO goods and no life rating.
issue.province_file_name: History file “{file}” does not follow the “<id> - <name>.txt” pattern.
explain.outcome.province_file_name: The game loads it anyway (it reads the leading number), but other tools may not recognise it.
issue.adjacency_unknown_province: The row names province {province}, which does not exist in definition.csv.
explain.title.adjacency_unknown_province: Why: adjacencies.csv uses province {province}, which does not exist
explain.outcome.adjacency_unknown_provin: That adjacency connects nothing: the strait, canal or pass will not work.
issue.adjacency_bad_type: Type “{type}” is not sea, impassable or canal.
explain.title.adjacency_bad_type: Why: “{type}” is not an adjacency type
explain.outcome.adjacency_bad_type: The game ignores the row or reads it as another type: the crossing will not do what is expected.
issue.adjacency_through_not_sea: The strait between {start} and {end} goes through province {province}, which is not sea.
explain.title.adjacency_through_not_sea: Why: Strait {start}–{end} crosses a land province
explain.outcome.adjacency_through_not_se: A strait is blocked by fleets in its sea province: over land it will never close as expected.
issue.terrain_sea_mismatch: Province {province} has terrain “{terrain}”, which does not match whether it is sea or land.
explain.title.terrain_sea_mismatch: Why: The terrain of province {province} does not match its type
explain.outcome.terrain_sea_mismatch: The game uses terrain for movement and combat: water on land (or land at sea) gives odd values.
